Prince Marth and his allied forces
were on the march to defend Altea.
On their path, they encountered the
Whitewings, led by Minerva, Princess
of Macedon—also known as the Red
Dragoon—blocking Marth's advance.
Witnessing the cowardly tactics of the
Grust soldiers serving by their side,
however, Minerva abandoned her
post, taking her troops with her...

No force on the continent of
Archanea compared to the Sable
Order of Knights in Grust, nor the
famed general who led them, Camus.
But the king of Grust was weak and
was forced into allegiance with an
empire of dragonkin. It was then that
they were forced to turn on the Holy
Kingdom of Archanea...

Camus and the Sable Order took the
holy capital, and the king was slain.
Princess Nyna of Archanea, however,
was able to escape with some help
from Camus. Swallowing her feelings
for him, she called for the aid of
Archanea's trusted allies. Marth heard
the call and answered, knowing his
time had come at last...

Just as Princess Nyna's luck was
about to run out, Marth and the
Altean army appeared! She then
entrusted Marth with the Fire
Emblem, which is granted by the
royal family only to a true champion,
one believed to have the power to
save the world...

Many treasures were kept within the
Millennium Court of Archanea—and
with them awaited Nyna's captured
vassals, guarded by Grust's knights
and a fire dragon of the empire...

With Camus's help, Nyna had been
able to escape her homeland—and
with Marth's help, she was able to
restore it. Fate had put Marth and
Camus on conflicting paths, both
leading toward Grust's ruin and
the eventual disappearance of the
famous Sable Knight...

The continent of Elibe had long been
at peace, keeping a delicate balance
between its nations. But the sudden
death of the king of Bern, one of its
major powers, ended that peace. The
new king, Zephiel, sought supremacy.
He worked together with dragons,
who had lost the battle for dominion
over Elibe long before. Together, they
began their invasions, dragging the
entire continent into war...

Bern's Wyvern General Narcian and
his wyvern knights invaded Lycia,
scattering its forces, leaving Roy in
need of aid. Etruria answered. With
the help of his teacher Cecilia, Mage
General of Etruria, Roy was able to
heroically beat back Bern's assault...

The Lycian forces, under Etruria's
protection, were dispatched to the
Western Isles with orders to subdue
a gang of bandits. Upon arrival, Roy
learned the local Etrurian nobles
were turning a blind eye to the
bandits in order to extort their own
people. As he pressed on, Roy met
a group of resistance fighters—and
along with them, a bard calling
himself Elffin...

As the League quelled corruption in
the Western Isles, an Etrurian faction
in collusion with Bern revolted and
captured the Etrurian king, who had
fallen ill with grief over news of the
death of his son, the prince. Roy,
knowing that Cecilia would be fighting
the uprising, left the Western Isles in
order to aid her—for not even she
could stand alone before Bern's king
and the Wyvern Generals...

After saving Cecilia, Roy and the
League's forces marched on the
Etrurian capital to end the uprising.
Perched in the throne room, Narcian
awaited their arrival, rallying his
troops to face the League head-on...

The long struggle for the capital came
to an end with Roy prevailing and
putting a halt to the uprising. In the
end, Elffin, the mysterious bard who
had given the League his support,
was revealed to be Myrddin, the
prince of Etruria who the king and
people had thought perished...

The Halidom of Ylisse was a country
of peace, ruled by the Exalt. One day,
Chrom, prince of Ylisse and leader
of the Shepherds, stumbled across
a person who had collapsed in the
middle of a field. The Shepherds
soon learned that this person, Robin,
who had lost all memory of the past,
was a great tactician. Robin joined
forces with the Shepherds, displaying
an incredible potential...

Still unprepared for the Risen
onslaught, Ylisse called for the aid of
its warlike neighbor, Regna Ferox.
It was Flavia, the East-Khan of Ferox,
who offered Ylisse her support, but
first she had to win a tournament to
prove herself worthy of being named
head Khan—so Chrom entered as her
champion. There, Chrom crossed
swords with Marth and emerged the
ultimate victor, sealing the alliance...

As Ylisse returned to stability, Mad
King Gangrel, the ruler of bordering
Plegia, used deceit to provoke Ylisse
into aggressive action. It was then
that Marth arrived and, claiming to
know the future, informed Chrom
that his sister Emmeryn, the exalt of
Ylisse, was at risk of assassination...

Chrom and company again sought
aid from Regna Ferox, spiriting the
exalt to safety. It was then that word
arrived of Gangrel's invasion of the
capital, Ylisstol. Though she faced
certain death, Emmeryn returned to
protect her people, entrusting the
symbol of the Ylissian royalty, the
Fire Emblem, to Chrom. Before long,
Ylisstol fell, and Emmeryn was taken...

Threatening to publicly execute
Emmeryn, Gangrel lured the Ylissian
forces to Plegia. Chrom and company
mounted a heroic rescue attempt, but
when Risen reinforcements arrived,
their plan was foiled. Gangrel then
offered to exchange Emmeryn's life
for the Fire Emblem—causing
Emmeryn to throw herself willingly
from a cliff to save others from
more suffering...

Though he had lost his beloved elder
sister, Chrom fought past his despair
to strike down Gangrel, thus ending
the war between Plegia and Ylisse.
Then, two years later, new invaders
approached from the west. Marth
again appeared in time to aid Chrom.
In doing so, Marth was revealed to
have been Lucina, Chrom's daughter,
all along—and she had traveled back
in time to prevent a dark future...

The kingdom of Zofia had grown
barren, and had been so for years.
Terrors spread over the land, and
the Rigelian Empire invaded. Zofia
was in a state of utter devastation
when Celica, a priestess of Novis,
set off on a journey to the temple
of Mila, the Earth Mother, seeking
a way to rescue the people...

As the newly appointed leader of the
Deliverance, Alm wasted no time in
mounting a counterattack. Pressing
the advance, the Deliverance moved
to retake Zofia Castle. Once it was
reclaimed, Alm announced he would
take the fight to the empire, putting
a stop to their conquest. Meanwhile,
his childhood friend Celica set off in
search of a more peaceful solution
to the conflict...

Alm and the Deliverance pursued the
defeated and retreating chancellor
Desaix as he fled from the retaken
castle. In his pursuit, Alm was forced
to confront Emperor Rudolf's
nephew, Berkut, who had been
stationed within Zofian territory.
Upon recognizing the birthmark on
Alm's hand, Berkut flew into a rage...

Alm and the Deliverance drove on,
crushing Berkut and his forces, who
waited at the empire's border. From
there, they proceeded to invade the
empire's territory. A witch who had
allied herself with Berkut then used
an illusion to lure the Deliverance to
Fear Mountain, but Alm defeated her
and freed her captives. One of the
captives then asked Alm to help her
lover, Ezekiel, an imperial general...

General Zeke, who had been forced
to fight after his lover, Tatiana, was
taken hostage, expressed his thanks
by joining the Deliverance in their
revolt against the empire. Upon sight
of the mark Alm bore on his hand,
Zeke revealed an order Rudolf gave
him: follow any man he met who
wore such a mark...

The Deliverance finally reached the
imperial castle and took it by storm,
defeating Rudolf in the process.
Recognizing Alm as his son, Rudolf
entrusted him with putting an end
to the mad god Duma. Reappearing,
Mycen reassured a confused Alm,
and confirmed that he was indeed
the true son of the emperor—and the
hero who had been prophesied.

Crimea, able to put up only a meager
resistance, was destroyed by Daein
when its king, Ashnard, launched an
assault. Princess Elincia, whose very
existence had been kept a secret, fled
to a friendly nearby country. In the
midst of her journey, she met the
Greil Mercenaries—and Ike, the son
of their leader...

Envoys from Begnion, including the
empress, Apostle Sanaki, were en
route to visit the princess when their
ship came under attack by pirates.
Learning of the attack, Ike sought to
rescue them, only to find that Sanaki
had disappeared in the chaos of the
fighting. When Ike finally found her,
he was surprised to learn how
young she was, given her station...

Ike and the mercenaries were then
summoned to the imperial capital.
Begnion had a long history of
enslaving and exploiting the laguz,
and even though such practices had
been officially outlawed, there were
still those who trafficked laguz.
Sanaki arranged a meeting between
the slavers, those who sought
emancipation, and Ike...

Sanaki had been targeting the slaver
ringleader, seeking to expose the
corruption of the Begnion nobility.
Sure enough, Ike found and rescued
the heron laguz prince who had long
been thought lost. Sanaki, shocked to
learn of his survival, explained the
story of the Serenes Massacre of
20 years prior...

Enraged over the assassination of the
previous Apostle and believing the
herons responsible, the Begnion
people had set the herons' home of
Serenes Forest ablaze. But the truth
was, the herons had been framed.
Sanaki knelt before the prince in her
people's stead and apologized for
their past trespasses...

The prince accepted Sanaki's apology
and used the Galdr of Rebirth to
restore the herons' home. Ike, having
forged a new bond between beorc
and laguz, impressed Begnion with
his efforts, earning their pledge of
support for the princess of Crimea.
The mercenaries then prepared to
enter a new battle, this time as the
Crimean Liberation Army.

The struggle between the peaceful
Hoshido and the militant Nohr was
reflected nowhere more strongly than
Corrin's heart. For one from Hoshido
but raised in Nohr, it was like having
two homes, two families—until Nohr's
King Garon assassinated Corrin's
mother. Forced to choose between
two brothers—Ryoma of Hoshido and
Xander of Nohr—Corrin sided with
Xander, but hoped to end their feud...

When King Garon visited a lively port
town to view a performance, Azura,
songstress and comrade of Corrin,
attempted to captivate and control
him with her mysterious song.
Xander's arrival, however, shifted
the balance of the situation. Backed
into a corner, Corrin was able to
emerge safely thanks to assistance
from Elise, the youngest of the royal
Nohrian siblings...

Corrin and company continued on,
advancing through Nohrian lands
under the ever-present cover of
darkness. Nohr's barren earth bore
only meager foodstuffs, forcing its
people to conquer to survive. Deep
in wooded Nohrian territory, the party
encountered and defeated Leo, who
revealed to them the conflict in his
heart—and their way forward...

Reaching the capital underground,
Corrin reunited with Elise. With her
guidance, they infiltrated the castle
only to be surprised by Camilla along
the way. Appealing to her heart,
Corrin and Elise desperately pleaded
with Camilla until she lowered her
axe and sent them on their way...

Defeating Iago with the aid of Leo,
Corrin then met Xander in the castle
and was forced to fight. Elise, not
wanting to see her siblings hurt one
another, put herself between the two
and was struck down by Xander's
blade. Even with her death, Xander
could not surrender, and ultimately
allowed himself to be defeated to
save his own Nohrian pride...

After so much sacrifice, Corrin finally
brought Garon low, but was able to
do so only with the aid of Azura, who
put all of her remaining strength into
her song before expiring from the
strain. On the day of Ryoma's
ascension to the throne, Corrin's
heart leaped with joy at the sight of
Azura in the lake where the two first
met—but in a blink, she was gone
again, vanishing into the waters.

On the continent of Jugdral, Prince
Kurth ruled Grannvale in the king's
stead, receiving aid from the duchies
Chalphy and Yngvi. Dissatisfied with
his rule, a faction aligned against the
prince began to take shape. When a
young lady of Yngvi was kidnapped
by barbarians from Verdane, Sigurd
of House Chalphy set out to
rescue her...

One day, when Grannvale's army was
away, forces from the neighboring
country of Verdane launched an
attack on Yngvi castle. Sigurd set out
to aid a lady of the castle, Edain, an
old friend of his. Approving of this
quest, Quan joined with Sigurd, and
the two made haste to the castle.
After the battle, the king expressed
his gratitude by granting Sigurd the
title of Holy Knight of Grannvale...

Though Sigurd helped protect the
castle, Edain had been abducted!
In pursuit, Sigurd took the fight to
Verdane. Eldigan was shocked to
learn Sigurd violated the border, but
after understanding Sigurd's reasons,
he promised to vouch for him in the
event of any protest from Agustria's
other nobility. So, Sigurd pushed on,
outmaneuvering and conquering
Verdane, annexing its territory...

In Agustria, anti-Grannvale sentiment
reached a fever pitch, and the king
ordered an invasion of Grannvale-
occupied Verdane. Eldigan sought
to convince Agustria's king toward
a peaceful path, but he was branded
a traitor and imprisoned...

With Grannvale and Agustria at war,
Sigurd reluctantly took the capital of
Agusti, forcing Agustria's surrender.
In doing so, he reunited with Eldigan,
freeing him. To ease Eldigan's fear,
Sigurd promised to withdraw within
the span of a year. Trusting his friend,
Eldigan took his injured king and went
to the north...

Despite Sigurd's intent, Grannvale did
not allow Agustria to return to
Agustrian control. Losing his
patience, the king of Agustria raised
an army. Though torn between love
for his country and love for his friend,
Eldigan risked it all for his honor,
proving himself worthy of the title
Holy Knight.

Amidst the chaos of the Grado
Empire's invasion of Renais, Ephraim,
prince of Renais, saves a young
manakete named Myrrh. Then, when
reunited with his sister, Eirika, they
all set out to mount a resistance
against Grado. Myrrh, however,
senses a threat. As daughter to the
guardian of the Darkling Woods,
where the Demon King is sealed
away, she knows danger lies ahead...

Princess Eirika of Renais escaped the
cruel imperial general Valter and fled
to the allied kingdom of Frelia. Alas,
the Sacred Stone of Frelia was lost,
destroyed at the hands of the empire.
To warn other nations and call for
aid against the threat of the empire,
Prince Innes of Frelia traveled toward
Jehanna, while Eirika volunteered to
visit the theocracy of Rausten...

With the ocean route to Rausten
blocked, Eirika's progress was
delayed. Elsewhere, on his journey
to Jehanna, Innes fell victim to
betrayal and was left in peril.
Hearing of this, Eirika rushed to his
aid, and the Princess of Renais and
the Prince of Frelia traveled together
from there...

The imperial general Glen moved on
Eirika's position to eliminate her, but
before he could, he is confronted by
the truth of the empire's deeds and
their lies to cover them up. Having
met Eirika in her youth and hearing
Innes's words, he chose to lower
his weapon. Shortly after, Glen was
killed for his failure by Valter, who
then told Glen's brother, Cormag,
it had been Eirika who killed Glen...

Just as Jehanna and its ruler, the
Queen of the White Dunes, were
about to fall to the empire, Eirika
was met by Cormag, who sought
vengeance for the death of his
brother. He was won over by her
sincerity, though, and instead
became her ally. After a long
struggle, Jehanna, too, fell to the
empire. With it fell their queen, and
their Sacred Stone was destroyed...

Eirika then found herself surrounded
by Valter's forces. As the situation
turned dire, Eirika's brother Ephraim
rushed in—and once they were free
from danger, he told her of the Dark
Stone and its malign control. They
decided the only way to contain the
evil of the Dark Stone is to use the
seals on the remaining Sacred Stones.
And with that, Eirika set out to her
homeland of Renais once more.

Medeus, the Shadow Dragon, rose
again and sought to restore the
Dolhr Empire. The resulting invasion
led to the loss of both Altea's king
and the sacred blade Falchion. The
young Prince Marth was forced to
flee, but at the behest of Princess
Nyna of Archanea, he returns to
recapture his homeland...

On the way to the Holy Kingdom
of Archanea, Marth learned that
Princess Maria, Minerva's sister,
was being held hostage by the Dolhr
Empire. One of Minerva's soldiers
revealed Minerva's plan for rebellion
to Marth—and that seeking his aid in
rescuing Maria was part of that plan...

The first king of Macedon, Iote, rode
a wyvern into battle in order to free
the enslaved. Prince Michalis had
been called the second coming of
Iote, and yet he joined forces with the
Dolhr Empire despite the protest of
his sister Minerva—solely to pursue
his own personal ambitions. Taking
their younger sister hostage, he had
forced Minerva to fight a war that
was not hers...

Marth, having faith in what he saw
behind Minerva's eyes, made his
way to the fortress where Maria was
held captive to rescue her—ignoring
the council of those who thought it
a trap. At Maria's return to safety,
Minerva expressed her thanks for
Marth's role in saving her sister,
and pledged to fight by his side...

Overcoming many trials on their way,
Marth and his companions eventually
arrived at the Macedon border. Marth
approached Minerva, concerned for
her mental state before the decisive
battle. Minerva, however, only wanted
to right the wrongs of her homeland,
and to do so by her own hand...

Unfazed by the might Macedon's
Dragoons boasted, Marth and Minerva
prevailed in battle, and Michalis was
believed slain. But several years later,
a coup in Macedon placed Minerva in
a dire position—and it is said that it
was none other than Michalis who
rescued her.

thought to have been defeated in

survived, however, and was revived
thousands of years later. Jahn, the
last fire dragon in Elibe, spent the
intervening years recovering from
the Scouring within the Dragon
Temple. When the Demon Dragon
was revived, he sensed her return...

away from Bern and sought the help
of the Lycian League. She hoped to
put a stop to the violence and find a
way back to peace. And in so doing,
placed her trust in Bern's enemies...

Although the Lycian League was
under the protection of Etruria, a
faction within it aligned with Bern.
Their wish to perform a coup served
to sow disorder within the League.
Taking advantage, Zephiel managed
to capture his sister, but she slipped
from his grasp with the aid of a loyal
retainer. The once-close siblings thus
parted, each unable to understand
the other...

defeat the coup-seeking faction
and recovered Etruria's capital.
Guinivere entrusted Roy, the leader
of the League's forces, with the Fire
Emblem as the fight against her
brother loomed ahead of them. With
it, Roy could gather the treasure of
Bern, the Binding Blade that once
defeated the dragons in ages past...

been the target of his father's ire and
resentment—which led to the king
planning Zephiel's assassination.

killed his father and took the throne.
As king, he wished to use his strength
to free the world of its treacherous
people and return it to the dragons...

capital and confronted Zephiel
himself. After a fierce battle, Zephiel
fell, and it seemed his ambitions
would go unfulfilled. The dark
priestess who had been ever at
his side, however, still remained
at large.

In the future witnessed by Lucina,
Chrom's daughter, Chrom was slain
by a traitor's hand, allowing the Fell
Dragon to be resurrected. The world
was plunged into despair. To save
both her father and the future, Lucina
traveled through time and prepared
her blade for battle, convinced
Validar would manipulate Robin into
killing Chrom...

A despicable scheme was hatched by
the tyrannical king of Plegia, which
was neighbor to Ylisse. The result
was the death of the exalt of Ylisse,
Chrom's elder sister. Plunged into
despair, Chrom's spirits were raised
by Robin, whose tactical prowess
aided in the downfall of Plegia's king
and the restoration of Ylisse. Chrom
and Robin grew close, sharing a bond
as if two halves of a whole...

It was then that the Empire of Valm
crossed the seas and descended
upon Ylisse. With few options left to
him, Chrom sought the aid of Plegia's
newly crowned king, Validar. But in
his court they met his hierophant...
who bore an uncanny likeness to
Robin. That night, Validar appeared
in Robin's mind and delivered the
shocking revelation that he was, in
truth, Robin's long-lost father...

At sea, the fleets of Valm and Ylisse
were matched ship-for-ship, but Valm
had twice the number of troops at
its disposal. Robin's genius, however,
gave Ylisse the upper hand. Emptying
half of their ships and loading them
with oil, Ylisse sent their fleet into
Valm's, incinerating their foes in a
daring surprise attack. Once ashore
in Valm, Chrom and company joined
the resistance against the Empire...

The Voice of the Divine Dragon, the
symbol and might of the resistance,
remained locked away within the
Mila Tree under the careful watch
of the Empire. When Chrom and
his fellows rescued the Voice, she
delivered a chilling prophecy of the
Fell Dragon's return. To prevent
catastrophe, they must collect the
five gemstones of the Fire Emblem
and perform the Awakening rite...

After a long struggle, the Valmese
Empire was quelled and Chrom then
turned to Plegia, who held the final
gemstone. Upon arrival, it became
clear the trials were not over—Validar
used his power to force Robin to
wrest the Fire Emblem from Chrom.
Chrom's daughter Lucina, armed with
knowledge of the future, realized that
Robin was her father's killer, and so
steeled herself to slay a beloved ally.

The Rigelian Empire was founded by
the god of strength, Duma. Berkut,
nephew of the emperor and next in
line for the throne, believed in only
his own power, however, and not in
any god's. Seeking to unify Valentia
under Rigelian rule, he made his way
to the kingdom of Zofia to hatch a
scheme with their chancellor, their
goal to spark a coup d'etat...

Ambushed by mysterious foes, Celica
was saved when a masked knight
came to her rescue. She then headed
toward Zofia Castle, where she was
reunited with her childhood friend,
Alm. With the intention of leading the
Deliverance, Alm hoped to put an
end to the conflict by military might.
Celica instead hoped for a divine
intervention. At an impasse, the two
had a falling out, and Celica left...

Celica learned that people were being
kidnapped and taken off to a thieves'
fortress. Aiming to defeat their leader,
Celica staged an assault on the
fortress and saved a priestess being
held there. The priestess, shocked to
see Celica's face, revealed she was
a priestess of Mila who had served
Celica's mother, the queen of Zofia...

Celica hurried on to Mila's temple,
but she arrived to find it devastated
by the Rigelian military, with no sign
of Mila. Just then, the masked knight
reappeared and gave Celica a circlet,
a keepsake of her mother's. Upon
receiving the gift, she swore to live
as the princess of Zofia from that
moment onward...

Celica and her entourage traveled
across Rigel after Mila, eventually
coming into contact with a priest of
Duma, god of strength. It was then
that Celica learned that both gods
were fated to fall, but she could offer
up her own soul to Duma to save
them. Celica lost herself in internal
conflict before being chastised by the
masked knight who then revealed he
was her long-lost older half-brother...

Celica, briefly reunited with Alm by
way of a sage's power, witnessed his
unwavering kindness and concern for
her, and resolved to bring an end to
the conflict for him. She returned to
the priest of Duma who had promised
Mila would be saved in exchange for
her soul, and she offered herself up
as a servant of Duma.

Daein invaded and laid waste to
Crimea, leading their princess to seek
out the protection of the mercenary
band led by Greil. Her flight was
noticed by the Black Knight, and he
pursued. Defeating Greil in combat,
the Black Knight demanded Greil give
up some artifact he was believed to
possess. Keeping the location of the
Black Knight's quarry secret, Greil
died as Ike carried him away...

Heeding the counsel of Gallia's king,
Elincia departed to Begnion to
request support in reconstructing
Crimea. The Greil Mercenaries
accepted the task of protecting the
princess along her journey...

The group encountered a myriad of
obstacles on their oversea journey
to Begnion, but finally, upon their
arrival, they were granted audience
with the empress apostle. There, the
apostle expressed her gratitude to
Ike and the other mercenaries for
exposing corruption within Begnion,
then pledged to support Elincia...

After an intense struggle, the Crimean
army overtook Daein's capital, but
Daein's king was nowhere to be
found. Elincia then turned her sights
on her homeland of Crimea, where
Ashnard was sure to wait, and set out
to confront him...

Elincia defeated the Daein army
at the great bridge spanning the
distance between the two countries.
At long last, she set foot in her
homeland, then convened with her
vassals who lay in wait there. News
spread of an unknown princess who
had defied Daein to save her home,
and the people awaited her return
with eager anticipation...

Laguz nations, recognizing the rapid
advance of the Crimean army, allied
themselves with Elincia, who, taking
to the battlefield herself, defeated
Ashnard at long last. Ike then stood
beside Elincia as she presented
herself to the people of Crimea, for
whom she had reclaimed a lasting
sense of peace.

Prince Corrin, born in peace-loving
Hoshido but raised in warlike Nohr,
was called a traitor by both for not
aligning with either. The songstress
Azura hurled herself into the
Bottomless Canyon and there
guided Corrin to the ruins of
a lost kingdom...

Corrin was sent out to suppress an
uprising in Cheve and was reunited
with Takumi, a prince of Hoshido,
along the way. Flying into a rage,
Takumi forced Corrin and company
into battle. It was then that Azura,
a songstress born in Nohr but raised
in Hoshido, sensed something off
about the brother she had known
to be so kind and caring...

One night, Corrin followed Azura to
the lakeside and learned two truths.
First, there is a hidden land between
worlds, and second, King Garon has
become a twisted shell of his former
self, a puppet to a maligned force.
To put an end to this deceit, Corrin
was to trick Garon into claiming the
throne of Hoshido and sitting on it,
which would reveal his true form...

Forced to conquer Hoshido to expose
the evil possessing Garon, Corrin and
the Nohrians marched on to their
goal. Reaching the Hoshidan capital
and mounting the wall that encircled
it, Corrin met and captured Takumi—
who was able to escape by seemingly
jumping to his death. Unable to locate
his body, however, Corrin had no
choice but to soldier on, anxious and
confused, to Hoshido's throne...

Forced to fight Ryoma, High Prince
of Hoshido, Corrin narrowly managed
to claim victory before facing the
final challenge: exposing Garon by
having him take the throne. Then, as
Garon's true form was revealed,
Corrin rallied the bewildered Nohrian
siblings, and they were able to finally
put an end to their possessed father...

Victory was cut short when Takumi,
now sustained by pure rage, returned
and loosed an arrow, striking Corrin.
But as Corrin lay dying, a vision of
Takumi's true self appeared and
reforged Corrin's weapon with his
Fujin Yumi. Returning to the living
world, Corrin then struck the final
blow against their enemy, ending the
long war. As peace returned, Azura
disappeared without a trace.

In the midst of chaos that consumed
Jugdral, the southern kingdom of
Thracia watched for an opportunity
to unify the lands to its north under
its rule. Quan, prince of Leonster,
a small country in the north, traveled
the desert to rescue his companion,
Sigurd—but along the way, Thracians
ambushed and killed Quan and
his wife...

Arvis, leader of the royal guard,
took to the battlefield, thanking
Sigurd with the gift of a silver sword
from the king. Sigurd, having routed
the barbarians and saved the maiden,
encountered a woman in the Spirit
Forest. Her name was Deirdre, and
the two quickly fell in love...

Together, Sigurd and Deirdre traveled
to a castle near the borderlands
between Grannvale, Agustria, and
Verdane. There, they lived happily
for a time. Before long, however, the
conflict surrounding Grannvale's
oppression of Verdane spread to
Agustria. Thus Sigurd marched to
battle with Deirdre at his side, hoping
to quell the violence. They remain for
some time, by order of the king...

Sigurd and Deirdre were eventually
blessed with a son. But Agustria,
growing dissatisfied with Grannvale's
military presence within its borders,
mustered its troops to reclaim its
territory. Amidst the ensuing battles,
Sigurd learned of Deirdre's sudden
disappearance, leaving their son
behind. Further, he was told of the
assassination of Prince Kurth—and
he and his father were suspected...

Framed by those who had deposed
the prince, Sigurd fled to Silesse for
protection. Before long, however,
his pursuers forced Silesse onto
the battlefield to defend the alleged
prince killers. Sigurd, determined to
clear the Chalphy name, set out
for Grannvale...

Repelling his foes, Sigurd advanced
on the capital, Belhalla, making his
triumphant return. It was only then
that he learned Deirdre awaited him,
having been robbed of her memory,
now married to Arvis. The revelation
made clear to Sigurd that all this had
been Arvis's grand design. Overtaken
by despair, Sigurd thus met with a
traitor's end: execution.

Lyon, the kind yet weak-willed
prince of Grado, grew up alongside
the royal twins of Renais, Ephraim
and Eirika. He researched the power
of Grado's Sacred Stone that sealed
the Demon King of ancient times,
hoping to one day use this power
for Grado's benefit...

Myrrh's dragonstone is taken
by General Selena, known as the
Fluorspar of the Grado Empire.
General Selena listens to what
Myrrh has to say about the ominous
presence she feels. But after Myrrh
explains it was a power that could
turn people evil, Selena simply
replies that if Myrrh wants her
dragonstone back, she will need
to take it back herself...

Even though Emperor Vigarde
seemed to have changed into
someone completely different than
the man he once was, Selena stayed
loyal to him. She tried in vain to make
him see reason. But when she comes
face-to-face with Ephraim, still she
remains loyal—to her dying breath.
Myrrh cannot help but wonder why
Selena had to die when she was a
good person deep down...

Ephraim advances on into the capital
and battles the emperor, but upon
Vigarde's defeat, his corpse turns to
ash. Ephraim then meets royal mage
and dark-magic researcher Knoll,
who had been imprisoned. The
emperor, Ephraim learns, had been
controlled by the power of the Dark
Stone, even in death...

Long ago, the Demon King was
sealed away, and Grado's Sacred
Stone was divided into the Sacred
Stone and the Dark Stone. The Dark
Stone held the Demon King's power,
and mages sought to harness it. But
when the Dark Stone was misused in
a plot to revive the Demon King, the
Sacred Stone was destroyed. So, to
stop the resurrection, Ephraim leads
his allies to the Darkling Woods...

When they arrive at the woods, Myrrh
hopes to be reunited with her father.
But at the sinister Black Temple, a
draco zombie attacks the party.
Myrrh fights, swallowing her feelings.
After the draco zombie is defeated,
and the party proceeds into the
Black Temple, Myrrh sheds quiet,
mournful tears.

Three powers vie for control of
Fódlan, a land under the watchful eye
of a goddess. At its center sits Garreg
Mach Monastery, where the Imperial
princess, the crown prince, and the
future Alliance leader study together
under the guidance of the archbishop
of the Church of Seiros...

In an act of rebellion, the Western
Church then attacks the monastery.
The aggressing force is led by the
masked Death Knight, and though
their assault ultimately fails, he does
manage to capture two students.
Tracking them in hopes of rescuing
the students, Byleth encounters yet
another masked enemy, the Flame
Emperor, who appears and prevents
any further exchange...

While responding to a shocking crisis
in Remire Village where inhabitants
were slaughtering each other, Byleth
and his students again discover the
Death Knight among the chaos. In
witness to the tragic scene, the Flame
Emperor offers an alliance to Byleth.
Upon Byleth's refusal, the Flame
Emperor warns Byleth this will be a
regretful decision and then slips
away...

Upon receiving a report that Demonic
Beasts have appeared, Byleth and
Jeralt rush to intervene. Jeralt is
moved by his son's courage, but soon
falls victim to the blade of an assassin
who had been masquerading as a
student. A tearful Byleth holds him in
his arms as he dies.

Byleth chases his father's killer to
the Sealed Forest, where entry is
ordinarily restricted. After being
ensnared in the trap that his enemies
set for him, Byleth becomes one with
the goddess and is born anew. As a
result, he is bid to enter the Holy
Tomb to receive enlightenment, but
he is followed shortly by the Flame
Emperor, troops in tow...

The Flame Emperor is then
revealed to be Edelgard, house
leader of the Black Eagles and
newly crowned emperor of the
Adrestian Empire. Forced to retreat
to imperial territory, Edelgard boldly
declares war on the Church of Seiros,
and Byleth is forced to choose
between Edelgard and the remaining
students defending the monastery.

Son of Quan, prince of Leonster. He musters
warriors to defeat the empire alongside Finn,
to whom he owes his life. Appears in Fire
Emblem: Thracia 776 / Genealogy of the
Holy War.

A noblewoman who inherits her father's last
wishes and leads the free city of Tarrah. She
is promised in marriage to Arion, prince of
Thracia. Appears in Fire Emblem: Thracia 776.

A bard who has traveled throughout Thracia,
observing an age of war and chaos. It is said
that his saga is beloved by many in the
generations that follow him. Appears in
Fire Emblem: Thracia 776.

Two brave warriors were responsible
for ending the War of Shadows—the
Coyote, Hardin, the king of Aurelis's
younger brother, and the Star and
Savior, Marth, from Altea, whom Nyna
entrusted with the Fire Emblem.

Planning to travel first to Archanea
and then to Altea, Marth learns that
his mother has been killed—and that
his sister was nowhere to be found.
What's more, the Dark Pontifex
Gharnef made off with the sword
Falchion. Thus, Marth marched
toward Dolhr to recover both his
sister and his father's sword...

In the Fane of Raman, storehouse
of ancient treasure, Marth saved
a manakete who was under the
influence of the Dark Pontifex's
control. This manakete was the last
surviving member of the Divine
Dragon tribe, and she decided to
grant her aid, allowing Marth to
gain both the Lightsphere and
the Starsphere...

Long ago, the dragon tribe was
punished by the gods, and they had
to seal their true forms within stones
so the people could live in peace.
Medeus upended the peace, founding
the Dolhr Empire and declaring war
on humankind. The Divine Dragon
Naga created Falchion from her fang,
and the first king of Altea used it to
defeat Medeus...

Gharnef was lying in wait at the
ancient temple of Thabes. Facing
him in battle, Marth was confronted
with the challenge of Gharnef's dark
magic, which nullified all attacks they
sent against him. But with the pairing
of the Lightsphere and Starsphere,
his dark magic was broken, and Marth
reclaimed Falchion and reunited with
his sister. At long last, only one final
hurdle remained...

Marth rode into Dolhr, Falchion in
hand, and struck down the Shadow
Dragon Medeus. With him died the
Empire itself, its dark influence
retreating from the land. The long
War of Shadows had finally come
to an end, and hope had been
restored to Archanea.
